intro: Hi! At work, on campus and with friends, people ask: what do you think? In this lesson you'll give your opinion with a clear reason, agree with other people, and disagree politely without sounding rude or saying nothing. Warm-up: what do you think about working from home?
teachingNotes: This is a speaking lesson that builds on what the learner already has: I think / I don't think + will (a2-will), because / so (a1-conjunctions, a2-linkers-sequence), because of, although and However, (b1-linkers-contrast-purpose), should and might (a2-modals-obligation, b1-modals-advice). Recap in a line, don't re-teach them. The shape to practise: opinion → reason → example (I think … because … For example, …). Topics: working from home, motorbikes vs public transport (KRL, TransJakarta, MRT), social media for kids, a four-day week.

Opinion starters: I think (the most common, menurut saya / saya rasa), In my opinion (a bit more formal, menurut pendapat saya; 'In my view' is also correct), I believe (stronger, more serious), Personally, … (secara pribadi), For me, … (bagi saya). Indonesian trap: 'Menurut saya' → *'According to me': it sounds strange to most English speakers; according to is for other people or sources (according to the news, according to Pak Hasan). Don't stack starters (*'In my opinion, I think …' says it twice: not a big mistake, just suggest one). A negative opinion is more natural with I don't think + a positive verb (I don't think it's a good idea), as in a2-will; accept 'I think it isn't'.

Justifying: because + subject + verb (because the traffic is terrible), because of + a noun (because of the traffic): the chain's rule, check it. The main reason is that … (accept 'the main reason is because' in speech, don't test it), For example, … (contohnya), That's why … (makanya / itulah sebabnya) comes AFTER the reason and introduces the opinion or result: 'The traffic is terrible. That's why I take the KRL.' 'because' and 'That's why' point in opposite directions. Balanced opinions with although / However, from the chain (Although motorbikes are fast, I think the KRL is safer).

Agreeing: I agree (with you / with Budi / with that), Exactly!, That's true, You're right, I think so too. The node's common error is *'I am agree with you' → 'I agree with you'. Why: agree is a verb (kata kerja, like like or want: I like it → I agree), so it takes no am / is / are. Indonesian 'saya setuju' feels like 'saya senang' (I am happy), which causes the am. Same rule everywhere: negative 'I don't agree' (not *'I'm not agree'), 'he doesn't agree', 'she agrees', question 'Do you agree?' (not *'Are you agree?'). Also agree WITH a person or idea (not *'agree to you'). 'I disagree' is correct but blunt.

Disagreeing politely: directness differs by culture. Many English speakers soften disagreement (acknowledge the other idea, then but + your view + a reason). Many Indonesians avoid open disagreement, especially with a boss or someone older (sungkan, 'iya, Pak' while thinking no); in an English meeting, silence or 'Yes, yes' is usually taken as agreement. Teach the middle way: say clearly that you see it differently, but softly: I see what you mean, but … / That's true, but … / I'm not sure about that. / I don't really agree, because … ('not really' softens: = kurang setuju, not 'sangat tidak setuju') / That's a good point. However, … (However starts a new sentence, as in the chain lesson; in speech it flows, don't correct the punctuation when they speak). Too direct for work: You're wrong. / That's not true. / No.

Limits: no second conditional (If I were you, I would …), no relative clauses, no passive, no reported speech (report what someone thinks with 'Budi thinks …'). Treat 'I'd say' and 'I see what you mean' as phrases to remember. When the learner gives an opinion, react to the idea first (agree or disagree politely, as a model), then correct ONE thing: usually 'I am agree', a missing reason, or 'because of' + subject + verb.

keyPoints.title: Give your opinion and say why
keyPoints.explanation: Start with I think, In my opinion, I believe (stronger), Personally, or For me. Not 'According to me': that's for other people (according to the news). Then give a reason: because + subject + verb, The main reason is that …, For example, …. That's why … comes after the reason (= makanya). For a 'no' opinion, say I don't think …

examples.en: In my opinion, the KRL is the best way to get to work in Jakarta.
examples.id: Menurut saya, KRL adalah cara terbaik untuk berangkat kerja di Jakarta.

examples.en: I think working from home is great because I save two hours a day.
examples.id: Menurut saya kerja dari rumah itu bagus karena saya hemat dua jam sehari.

examples.en: The roads are too busy in the morning. That's why I take the MRT.
examples.id: Jalanan terlalu ramai di pagi hari. Makanya saya naik MRT.

id.title: Sampaikan pendapatmu dan katakan alasannya
id.explanation: Mulai dengan I think, In my opinion, I believe (lebih kuat), Personally, atau For me. Bukan 'According to me': itu untuk orang atau sumber lain (according to the news = menurut berita). Lalu beri alasan: because + subjek + kata kerja, The main reason is that …, For example, …. That's why … datang setelah alasannya (= makanya). Untuk pendapat 'tidak', katakan I don't think …

keyPoints.title: Agree and disagree politely
keyPoints.explanation: Agree: I agree (with you), Exactly!, That's true, You're right. agree is a verb, so no am: 'I am agree' is wrong, and the negative is I don't agree. Disagree softly: first show you heard the idea, then but + your view + a reason: I see what you mean, but … / That's true, but … / I'm not sure about that. / I don't really agree, because …. 'You're wrong' is too direct, and saying nothing sounds like you agree.

examples.en: I agree with you. A four-day week sounds great.
examples.id: Saya setuju denganmu. Empat hari kerja seminggu kedengarannya bagus.

examples.en: I see what you mean, but motorbikes can be dangerous in heavy rain.
examples.id: Saya paham maksudmu, tapi motor bisa berbahaya saat hujan deras.

examples.en: I don't really agree, because kids need time away from screens.
examples.id: Saya kurang setuju, karena anak-anak butuh waktu jauh dari layar.

id.title: Setuju dan tidak setuju dengan sopan
id.explanation: Setuju: I agree (with you), Exactly!, That's true, You're right. agree adalah kata kerja, jadi tanpa am: 'I am agree' salah, dan bentuk negatifnya I don't agree. Tidak setuju dengan lembut: tunjukkan dulu bahwa kamu mendengar idenya, lalu but + pendapatmu + alasan: I see what you mean, but … / That's true, but … / I'm not sure about that. / I don't really agree, because …. 'You're wrong' terlalu langsung, dan diam saja terdengar seperti kamu setuju.

assessment.rubric: Full marks: a soft start that shows you heard the idea or that you see it a bit differently (I see what you mean, but … / That's true, but … / I'm not sure about that / I don't really agree). 'I disagree' = 60 (clear, but blunt at a meeting). 'You're wrong' or 'That's not true' = 20 (too direct). 'I am not agree' = 20. 'Yes, Bu' / 'OK' / 'I agree' = 0 (it doesn't show any disagreement).

blocks.text:
An **opinion** is what you think about something (*pendapat*). You already know **I think** from A2 (*I think it will rain*). Here are five ways to start, from the most common to the most serious:
- **I think …** (*menurut saya / saya rasa*): the everyday choice.
- **In my opinion, …** (*menurut pendapat saya*): a bit more formal, good at work or in class. *In my view* means the same.
- **Personally, …** (*secara pribadi*): this is MY view, other people may think differently.
- **For me, …** (*bagi saya*): friendly and simple.
- **I believe …** (*saya yakin / saya percaya*): stronger and more serious.

After the starter comes a normal sentence: a **subject** (who or what: *the KRL, kids, working from home*) + a **verb** (*is, need, saves*).

id.text:
**Opinion** adalah apa yang kamu pikirkan tentang sesuatu (*pendapat*). Kamu sudah tahu **I think** dari A2 (*I think it will rain*). Ini lima cara untuk memulai, dari yang paling umum sampai yang paling serius:
- **I think …** (*menurut saya / saya rasa*): pilihan sehari-hari.
- **In my opinion, …** (*menurut pendapat saya*): sedikit lebih formal, cocok di kantor atau di kelas. *In my view* artinya sama.
- **Personally, …** (*secara pribadi*): ini pandangan **saya** sendiri, orang lain mungkin berpikir lain.
- **For me, …** (*bagi saya*): ramah dan sederhana.
- **I believe …** (*saya yakin / saya percaya*): lebih kuat dan lebih serius.

Setelah pembukanya, datang kalimat biasa: **subjek** (siapa atau apa: *the KRL, kids, working from home*) + **kata kerja** (*is, need, saves*).

blocks.text:
Indonesian trap: **Menurut saya** is NOT *According to me*. Most English speakers find *According to me, …* strange. **according to** is for other people or sources: *according to the news, according to Pak Hasan* (*menurut berita, menurut Pak Hasan*). For yourself, say **I think** or **In my opinion**.
Also choose **one** starter: *In my opinion, I think …* says the same thing twice.

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **Menurut saya** BUKAN *According to me*. Kebanyakan penutur bahasa Inggris merasa *According to me, …* terdengar aneh. **according to** dipakai untuk orang atau sumber lain: *according to the news, according to Pak Hasan* (*menurut berita, menurut Pak Hasan*). Untuk dirimu sendiri, katakan **I think** atau **In my opinion**.
Pilih juga **satu** pembuka saja: *In my opinion, I think …* mengatakan hal yang sama dua kali.

blocks.prompt: Which is the most natural way to say 'Menurut saya, TransJakarta lebih murah'?
options: According to me, TransJakarta is cheaper.
I am think TransJakarta is cheaper.
blocks.explain: For your own opinion, use **I think** (or In my opinion). *According to me* sounds strange: according to is for other people or sources. *think* is a verb, so there's no *am* before it.

id.prompt: Mana cara paling alami untuk mengatakan 'Menurut saya, TransJakarta lebih murah'?
id.explain: Untuk pendapatmu sendiri, pakai **I think** (atau In my opinion). *According to me* terdengar aneh: according to dipakai untuk orang atau sumber lain. *think* adalah kata kerja, jadi tidak ada *am* di depannya.

blocks.text:
An opinion with no reason sounds weak. A good answer has **three parts**: **opinion → reason → example**.
- **because** + subject + verb: *I like working from home **because I save** two hours a day.*
- **because of** + a noun (*kata benda*: a thing, like *the traffic, the rain*): *I'm often late **because of the traffic**.* (You learnt this difference in the linkers lesson.)
- **The main reason is that** + subject + verb (*alasan utamanya adalah …*): *The main reason is that the roads are too busy.*
- **For example, …** (*contohnya, …*): a real case that shows you're right.
- **That's why …** (*makanya / itulah sebabnya*): the reason comes **first**, then *That's why* + your opinion or decision. *The roads are too busy. **That's why** I take the KRL.*

To show you see both sides, use **although** or **However,**: *Although motorbikes are fast, I think the KRL is safer.*

id.text:
Pendapat tanpa alasan terdengar lemah. Jawaban yang bagus punya **tiga bagian**: **pendapat → alasan → contoh**.
- **because** + subjek + kata kerja: *I like working from home **because I save** two hours a day.*
- **because of** + kata benda (benda atau hal, seperti *the traffic, the rain*): *I'm often late **because of the traffic**.* (Kamu sudah belajar bedanya di pelajaran kata penghubung.)
- **The main reason is that** + subjek + kata kerja (*alasan utamanya adalah …*): *The main reason is that the roads are too busy.*
- **For example, …** (*contohnya, …*): kasus nyata yang menunjukkan kamu benar.
- **That's why …** (*makanya / itulah sebabnya*): alasannya datang **lebih dulu**, lalu *That's why* + pendapat atau keputusanmu. *The roads are too busy. **That's why** I take the KRL.*

Untuk menunjukkan kamu melihat dua sisi, pakai **although** atau **However,**: *Although motorbikes are fast, I think the KRL is safer.*

blocks.text:
**because** and **That's why** point in opposite directions:
- *I take the KRL **because** the roads are busy.* (opinion/decision → reason)
- *The roads are busy. **That's why** I take the KRL.* (reason → opinion/decision)
Indonesian *makanya* = **That's why**, not *because*. And keep the rule from earlier lessons: one linker per sentence (not *Because the roads are busy, so I take the KRL*).

id.text:
**because** dan **That's why** menunjuk ke arah yang berlawanan:
- *I take the KRL **because** the roads are busy.* (pendapat/keputusan → alasan)
- *The roads are busy. **That's why** I take the KRL.* (alasan → pendapat/keputusan)
*Makanya* dalam bahasa Indonesia = **That's why**, bukan *because*. Dan tetap ingat aturan dari pelajaran sebelumnya: satu kata penghubung per kalimat (bukan *Because the roads are busy, so I take the KRL*).

blocks.prompt: Complete: Dimas likes working in the office ___ he can talk to his team face to face.
blocks.explain: After the gap comes a subject + verb (*he can talk*), and it's the reason, so use **because**. *because of* needs a noun (*because of his team*). *That's why* goes after a reason, at the start of a new sentence.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas likes working in the office ___ he can talk to his team face to face.
id.explain: Setelah titik-titik ada subjek + kata kerja (*he can talk*), dan itu alasannya, jadi pakai **because**. *because of* butuh kata benda (*because of his team*). *That's why* datang setelah alasan, di awal kalimat baru.

material.title: Agreeing: I agree, not I am agree

blocks.text:
When you share someone's opinion, say so:
- **I agree.** / **I agree with you.** (*saya setuju (denganmu)*). agree **with** a person or an idea: *I agree with Budi. I agree with that.*
- **Exactly!** (*betul sekali! persis!*): strong agreement.
- **That's true.** (*memang benar*)
- **You're right.** (*kamu benar*)
- **I think so too.** (*saya juga berpikir begitu*)

Why no *am*? **agree** is a **verb** (*kata kerja*: an action word, like *like, want, think*). You say *I like it*, not *I am like it*, so you say **I agree**, not *I am agree*.

id.text:
Kalau kamu sependapat dengan seseorang, katakan:
- **I agree.** / **I agree with you.** (*saya setuju (denganmu)*). agree **with** orang atau ide: *I agree with Budi. I agree with that.*
- **Exactly!** (*betul sekali! persis!*): sangat setuju.
- **That's true.** (*memang benar*)
- **You're right.** (*kamu benar*)
- **I think so too.** (*saya juga berpikir begitu*)

Kenapa tanpa *am*? **agree** adalah **kata kerja** (kata yang menunjukkan tindakan, seperti *like, want, think*). Kamu bilang *I like it*, bukan *I am like it*, jadi kamu bilang **I agree**, bukan *I am agree*.

blocks.text:
Indonesian trap: *saya setuju* feels like *saya senang* (*I am happy*), so many learners say `I am agree` ✗. But **happy** is an adjective (a describing word) and needs *am*; **agree** is a verb and doesn't. Treat it like *like*:
- *I like* → **I agree**
- *I don't like* → **I don't agree**
- *Do you like …?* → **Do you agree?**
- *She likes* → **She agrees**

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *saya setuju* terasa seperti *saya senang* (*I am happy*), jadi banyak pelajar bilang `I am agree` ✗. Tapi **happy** adalah kata sifat (kata yang menggambarkan) dan butuh *am*; **agree** adalah kata kerja dan tidak butuh *am*. Perlakukan seperti *like*:
- *I like* → **I agree**
- *I don't like* → **I don't agree**
- *Do you like …?* → **Do you agree?**
- *She likes* → **She agrees**

options: Pak Hasan is agree with Sari.
blocks.explain: **agree** is a verb, so there's no *is*. And Pak Hasan = he, so the verb takes **-s**: **agrees**, just like *he likes*.

id.explain: **agree** adalah kata kerja, jadi tidak ada *is*. Dan Pak Hasan = he, jadi kata kerjanya mendapat **-s**: **agrees**, sama seperti *he likes*.

id.title: Menyatakan setuju: I agree, bukan I am agree

blocks.text:
How directly people disagree is different in every culture.
- **Many English speakers soften disagreement.** They show they heard the other idea first, then say *but* + their view + a reason. *You're wrong* or *That's not true* sounds rude in most workplaces.
- **Many Indonesians avoid open disagreement**, especially with a boss or someone older (*sungkan*). They stay quiet or say *Iya, Pak* while thinking *no*. In an English meeting, silence or *Yes, yes* usually means **you agree**, so nobody hears your real view.

**The middle way:** say clearly that you see it differently, but softly. 1) Show you heard the idea. 2) **but** + your view. 3) A reason.
*I see what you mean, but I think motorbikes are dangerous in the rain.*

id.text:
Seberapa langsung orang menyatakan tidak setuju berbeda di setiap budaya.
- **Banyak penutur bahasa Inggris melembutkan ketidaksetujuan.** Mereka menunjukkan dulu bahwa mereka mendengar ide orang lain, lalu bilang *but* + pandangan mereka + alasan. *You're wrong* (kamu salah) atau *That's not true* (itu tidak benar) terdengar kasar di kebanyakan tempat kerja.
- **Banyak orang Indonesia menghindari ketidaksetujuan terbuka**, apalagi dengan atasan atau orang yang lebih tua (*sungkan*). Mereka diam atau bilang *Iya, Pak* padahal dalam hati *tidak*. Di rapat berbahasa Inggris, diam atau *Yes, yes* biasanya berarti **kamu setuju**, jadi tidak ada yang mendengar pendapatmu yang sebenarnya.

**Jalan tengahnya:** katakan dengan jelas bahwa kamu melihatnya berbeda, tapi dengan lembut. 1) Tunjukkan kamu mendengar idenya. 2) **but** + pandanganmu. 3) Alasan.
*I see what you mean, but I think motorbikes are dangerous in the rain.*

rows.id: Saya kurang setuju, karena beberapa pekerjaan butuh lima hari.

rows.en: That's a good point. However, a four-day week is hard for shops.
rows.id: Itu poin yang bagus. Namun, empat hari kerja seminggu sulit untuk toko.

rows.en: You're wrong. That's not true.
rows.id: Kamu salah. Itu tidak benar.

id.note: terlalu langsung: hindari di tempat kerja

blocks.text: **really** makes a negative **softer**, not stronger: **I don't really agree** = *saya kurang setuju*, not *saya sangat tidak setuju*. And **I disagree** is correct, but it's blunt: add a soft start or a reason. Remember from the linkers lesson: in writing, **However,** starts a new sentence (*That's a good point. However, …*).

id.text: **really** membuat kalimat negatif jadi **lebih lembut**, bukan lebih kuat: **I don't really agree** = *saya kurang setuju*, bukan *saya sangat tidak setuju*. Dan **I disagree** itu benar, tapi terdengar blak-blakan: tambahkan pembuka yang lembut atau alasan. Ingat dari pelajaran kata penghubung: dalam tulisan, **However,** memulai kalimat baru (*That's a good point. However, …*).

blocks.prompt: Your friend says: 'Kids should get a phone when they're six.' You disagree. Which reply is clear AND polite?
options: I'm not sure about that. I think six is too young.
blocks.explain: **I'm not sure about that** softly says you see it differently, and then you give your view. *Hmm, yes, maybe* hides what you think, so your friend will think you agree. *That's not true. You're wrong.* is too direct.

id.prompt: Temanmu bilang: 'Kids should get a phone when they're six.' Kamu tidak setuju. Balasan mana yang jelas DAN sopan?
id.explain: **I'm not sure about that** dengan lembut menunjukkan kamu melihatnya berbeda, lalu kamu memberi pandanganmu. *Hmm, yes, maybe* menyembunyikan pendapatmu, jadi temanmu akan mengira kamu setuju. *That's not true. You're wrong.* terlalu langsung.

id.title: Tidak setuju dengan sopan: jalan tengah

blocks.text: Rina and Budi are talking about a four-day work week at lunch. Find the **opinion starters**, the **reasons and examples**, and how they **agree** and **disagree politely**.

id.text: Rina dan Budi sedang membicarakan empat hari kerja seminggu saat makan siang. Temukan **pembuka pendapat**, **alasan dan contoh**, dan cara mereka **setuju** dan **tidak setuju dengan sopan**.

rows.en: Rina: Personally, I think a four-day week is a great idea.
rows.id: Rina: Secara pribadi, menurut saya empat hari kerja seminggu itu ide bagus.

rows.en: Rina: The main reason is that people need more time with their families.
rows.id: Rina: Alasan utamanya adalah orang butuh lebih banyak waktu dengan keluarga.

rows.en: Budi: That's true. But I'm not sure about it for our team.
rows.id: Budi: Memang benar. Tapi saya kurang yakin untuk tim kita.

rows.en: Budi: Our clients call us every day. For example, Pak Hasan calls on Fridays.
rows.id: Budi: Klien kita menelepon setiap hari. Contohnya, Pak Hasan menelepon tiap hari Jumat.

rows.en: Rina: You're right. We might need a different plan for our team.
rows.id: Rina: Kamu benar. Kita mungkin butuh rencana lain untuk tim kita.

blocks.prompt: In the discussion, how does Budi disagree?
options: He agrees with part of her idea, then gives a reason and an example.
He doesn't say what he thinks.
blocks.explain: Budi says **That's true** (he agrees with part of Rina's idea), then **I'm not sure about it** + a reason and **For example, …**. That's the middle way: clear, but soft.

id.prompt: Dalam diskusi itu, bagaimana Budi menyatakan tidak setuju?
id.explain: Budi bilang **That's true** (dia setuju dengan sebagian ide Rina), lalu **I'm not sure about it** + alasan dan **For example, …**. Itulah jalan tengahnya: jelas, tapi lembut.
options: Dia menyetujui sebagian idenya, lalu memberi alasan dan contoh.

id.intro: Halo! Di kantor, di kampus dan dengan teman, orang sering bertanya: menurutmu bagaimana? Di pelajaran ini kamu akan menyampaikan pendapat dengan alasan yang jelas, menyatakan setuju dengan orang lain, dan tidak setuju dengan sopan tanpa terdengar kasar atau diam saja. Pemanasan: apa pendapatmu tentang kerja dari rumah?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa saya tidak boleh bilang 'According to me'?
Bagaimana cara tidak setuju dengan atasan secara sopan dalam bahasa Inggris?

assessment.go-1: Lengkapi dengan satu kata. Rina sedang membicarakan media sosial untuk anak-anak: 'In my ___, children under 13 shouldn't have social media accounts, because they can meet strangers online.'
assessment.go-2: Lengkapi dengan That's why atau because: Many people in Jakarta spend three hours a day in traffic. ___ I think working from home two days a week is a good idea.
assessment.go-3: Beri alasan. Selesaikan pendapat Sari dengan alasan singkat dalam bahasa Inggris yang punya subjek dan kata kerja (3–8 kata). Tulis hanya bagian setelah because: I prefer the KRL to a motorbike because ___
assessment.go-4: Perbaiki kesalahannya: My manager is not agree with the new plan.
assessment.go-5: Rekan kerjamu bilang: 'The coffee in the new office canteen is too expensive.' Kamu setuju. Tulis balasan singkat (1–4 kata) dalam bahasa Inggris untuk mengatakannya.
assessment.go-6: Di rapat, Bu Ani bilang: 'I think we should stop all online meetings. They're a waste of time.' Kamu tidak setuju sebagian. Tulis frasa sopan (2–6 kata) dalam bahasa Inggris untuk memulai balasanmu, sebelum kamu memberi alasan.
